title: How many lines does each complete graph have?
description: The lines in the complete graphs with two to six dots are counted and give one, three, six, ten and fifteen. A new dot is joined to every dot before it, which adds one more line each time.
teaching_notes: One idea: each new dot is joined to all the dots before it, so it adds one more line than the last new dot did. Watch for students who add the same number of lines each time.

source: Figure it Out Q2 (Try This), p.11
video_script.why: The child counts the lines of each complete graph and explains the counts by what each new dot adds, as the solved example counts what each new triangle adds.
video_script.substitution: A new dot joined to all the dots before it adds lines, in place of a new triangle adding sticks.
video_script.anchor: the complete graphs with two to six dots, with the number of lines written under each
video_script.payoff_line: The lines are the triangular numbers, one, three, six, ten and fifteen

final_answer.spoken: one, three, six, ten and fifteen, the triangular numbers

maths_rules: a complete graph has a line between every two dots
lines of the graphs with 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 dots: 1, 3, 6, 10, 15
the new dot adds 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 lines in turn
check: 6 dots x 5 others = 30 line ends, 30 / 2 = 15 lines
video_script.design: The complete graphs stand in a row with the lines counted under each. A new dot joins the earlier dots, and the new lines are lit and counted.
